summary.text: A 47-year-old woman presented with best-corrected visual acuity of 20/20 in the right eye and 20/40 in the left eye and recent onset of metamorphopsia in the left eye. Family history was significant for Best macular dystrophy in two siblings and other paternal-side relatives.

Anterior segment examination was unremarkable. Fundus examination showed pigmentary changes at the posterior pole in both eyes and yellowish subretinal material in the left eye. Fluorescein angiography showed bilateral early macular hyperfluorescence with late dye leakage in the left eye, and SD-OCT showed a subfoveal detachment in the right eye and retinal thickening with subretinal fluid in the left eye. She was diagnosed with Best macular dystrophy complicated by choroidal neovascularization in the left eye.

She underwent four intravitreal bevacizumab injections, with resolution of subretinal fluid after the second injection. No recurrence of CNV activity was noted over 8 years of follow-up, with stable SD-OCT. At the last visit, BCVA was 20/70 in the right eye and 20/50 in the left eye, follow-up OCT showed sustained resolution of subretinal fluid in the left eye, and OCTA did not demonstrate any clear neovascular network on outer retinal slabs.

summary.text: A 34-year-old woman presented with decreasing vision in the right eye, with best-corrected visual acuity of 20/40 in the right eye and 20/30 in the left eye. Multiple family members, including her father, were diagnosed with Best macular dystrophy.

Fundus examination showed large bilateral vitelliform detachments, subretinal fibrosis and pigmentary changes. Fluorescein angiography showed central dye staining and late pooling within the vitelliform lesions, SD-OCT showed a shallow subfoveal optically empty space with a hyperreflective RPE detachment in both eyes, and en-face OCTA revealed a neovascular network in the outer retinal slabs bilaterally.

She received two monthly bevacizumab injections in the right eye. Because there was no improvement in vision, subretinal fluid or CNV size, further intravitreal treatment was deferred with a plan to observe closely. Her last BCVA was 20/70 in the right eye and 20/25 in the left eye, with a similar macular appearance on follow-up.

summary.text: A 71-year-old man presented with BCVA of 20/150 and eccentric vision in both eyes. His ocular history was positive for EOG-proven Best macular dystrophy with onset in his 5th decade of life, and he had a strong family history of the disease.

Fundus examination showed bilateral RPE and retinal atrophy in the posterior pole, with subfoveal fibrosis in the right eye and parafoveal fibrosis in the left eye. Short-wavelength autofluorescence showed a hyper-FAF ring with multiple hypo-FAF patches corresponding to RPE atrophy, SD-OCT showed dense hyperreflective lesions with extensive back-scattering, and FA showed early and late hyperfluorescence.

He was managed conservatively and followed for 11 years. At the last visit OCTA showed large CNV lesions in both eyes with no exudation associated with the CNV in either eye, described in the discussion as bilateral inactive CNV in advanced atrophic disease.

Figure 2
Multimodal imaging of Case 2 showing a choroidal neovascular membrane in both the right eye (RE) and left eye (LE). (A,B). Fundus color picture showing large bilateral vitelliform detachment, subretinal fibrosis, and pigmentary changes. (C,D). The left, asymptomatic eye showed a large network with large caliber vessels that corresponded to the central fibrotic elements clinically and on the fundus photo.
